title: A Weekend in Jaipur: Forts, Food and Pink Streets
author: Manzil Bharat Team
excerpt: How to make the most of 48 hours in the Pink City - Amber Fort at sunrise, street food in Johari Bazaar, and where to stay on a budget.
content:
Jaipur, the Pink City, is perfect for a weekend getaway. Here's a no-fuss itinerary to help you cover the highlights without rushing.

Day 1: Forts and Old City

  • Sunrise (6:30 AM): Start at Amber Fort. Go early to beat the crowds and heat.
  • Morning: Explore the City Palace and Jantar Mantar nearby.
  • Afternoon: Get lost in Johari Bazaar - look for block prints and lac bangles.
  • Evening: Head to Nahargarh Fort for the classic sunset view over Jaipur.

Day 2: Palaces and Food

  • Morning: Visit Hawa Mahal and take photos from the street opposite.
  • Lunch: Try a Rajasthani thali at Laxmi Misthan Bhandar (LMB).
  • Afternoon: Explore the Albert Hall Museum or wander through the bazaars.
  • Evening: End with pyaaz kachori from Rawat Mishthan Bhandar.

Tips

Use auto-rickshaws for short distances, carry water, and wear comfortable walking shoes. Most monuments are closed on select days, so check timings in advance.

title: Goa Beyond Baga: Quiet Beaches Worth Visiting
author: Manzil Bharat Team
excerpt: Skip the crowds and discover South Goa's serene beaches - Palolem, Agonda, and Cola Beach offer the peace most tourists miss.
content:
While North Goa's party scene draws crowds, South Goa is where you'll find tranquil beaches, empty shores, and incredible seafood.

Must-Visit Beaches

  • Palolem Beach: A crescent-shaped beach with calm waters, perfect for swimming and kayaking.
  • Agonda Beach: Quiet and pristine, with beach shacks serving fresh catch of the day.
  • Cola Beach: A hidden gem with a freshwater lagoon where you can swim and relax.

Where to Eat

Try Vinayak Family Restaurant for their fish thali, or head to a local shack for grilled kingfish with rice and curry.

Getting Around

Rent a scooter to explore South Goa at your own pace. Roads are scenic and parking is easy at most beaches.

title: Old Delhi Street Food: A Hunger-Filled Walk
author: Manzil Bharat Team
excerpt: From parathas in Paranthe Wali Gali to kebabs near Jama Masjid, here's where to eat your way through Old Delhi.
content:
Old Delhi is a food lover's paradise. The best way to explore it is on foot (or by rickshaw) with an empty stomach.

Must Try

  • Paranthe Wali Gali: Stuffed parathas with everything from potatoes to rabri. Go early to avoid long queues.
  • Karim's near Jama Masjid: Legendary for mutton korma, seekh kebabs, and sheermal.
  • Chandni Chowk Chaat: Don't miss aloo tikki, golgappe, and dahi bhalla from the street vendors.
  • Kake Di Hatti: Known for their massive naans and rich curries.

Tips for Foodies

Go with a friend so you can share dishes. Carry cash as many vendors don't accept cards. Stick to busy stalls - they're usually busy for a reason.

title: Manali to Sissu: A High-Altitude Road Trip
author: Manzil Bharat Team
excerpt: Drive through the Atal Tunnel to reach the cold desert of Lahaul. Stunning views, mountain passes, and adventure await.
content:
The drive from Manali to Sissu via the Atal Tunnel is one of India's most spectacular road trips. In just a couple of hours, you go from lush green valleys to stark mountain desert.

Route Highlights

  • Atal Tunnel: The 9.02 km tunnel at 10,000 ft saves hours and opens up Lahaul year-round.
  • Sissu: A small village with views of the Chandra River and snow-capped peaks. Great for a quick stop and tea.
  • Solang Valley: Worth a detour if you're interested in paragliding or zorbing.

Practical Tips

Check weather conditions before going - high altitude can have sudden changes. Carry warm layers even in summer. Fuel up in Manali as petrol pumps are limited beyond the tunnel.

title: Varanasi: Ghats, Ganga Aarti and Timeless Traditions
author: Manzil Bharat Team
excerpt: Experience the spiritual heart of India - dawn boat rides, evening aartis, and the ancient lanes of Kashi.
content:
Varanasi, also known as Kashi, is one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities. It's chaotic, colorful, and deeply spiritual all at once.

Must-Do Experiences

  • Sunrise Boat Ride: Start your day with a rowboat ride from Assi Ghat to Manikarnika Ghat. The morning light is magical.
  • Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh: Don't miss the evening aarti - synchronized prayers, bells, and lamps create an unforgettable atmosphere.
  • Wander the Ghats: Each ghat has its own story. Take time to walk from Assi to Dashashwamedh.
  • Day Trip to Sarnath: Where Buddha gave his first sermon, just 10 km from Varanasi.

Food Recommendations

Try tamatar chaat at Kashi Chat Bhandar, malai lassi at Blue Lassi Shop, and Banarasi paan for a traditional ending.
